headline: 3 police officers withdrawn after national cricketer Naim Hasan alleged assault
summary: The BCB and fellow cricketers have condemned the harassment of the spinner in Chattogram, demanding a thorough investigation and justice.
details: National team spinner Naim Hasan alleged he was assaulted and harassed by individuals identifying themselves as detectives in Chattogram on Friday night.

Naim reported that after a flight delay, he took an autorickshaw near Lalkhan Bazar, where police signaled the vehicle to stop. He claims he was pushed by the neck and struck with a baton and a pipe despite identifying himself as a national cricketer.
The 26-year-old spinner alleged that he was later taken to a police station and faced further harassment inside the station chief's room.
The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) expressed deep concern and condemned the treatment as unacceptable, calling for a thorough and impartial investigation.
The Cricketers' Welfare Association (CWAB) and top cricketers including Litton Kumer Das, Mushfiqur Rahim, and Mehidy Hasan Miraz have also demanded exemplary punishment for those responsible.
Following the incident, three police officers, including a Sub-Inspector (SI), have been withdrawn from their posts as part of the initial action.
Naim Hasan holds the record for the youngest player to take a five-wicket haul on Test debut and is scheduled to tour Zimbabwe later this month.
caption:
A national cricketer was allegedly beaten with a baton and a pipe by police in Chattogram. Now, the cricket fraternity is demanding justice.

National team spinner Naim Hasan alleged he was assaulted and harassed by individuals identifying themselves as detectives in Chattogram on Friday night.

Naim reported that after a flight delay, he took an autorickshaw near Lalkhan Bazar, where police signaled the vehicle to stop. He claims he was pushed by the neck and struck with a baton and a pipe despite identifying himself as a national cricketer.

The 26-year-old spinner alleged that he was later taken to a police station and faced further harassment inside the station chief's room.

The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) expressed deep concern and condemned the treatment as unacceptable, calling for a thorough and impartial investigation.

The Cricketers' Welfare Association (CWAB) and top cricketers including Litton Kumer Das, Mushfiqur Rahim, and Mehidy Hasan Miraz have also demanded exemplary punishment for those responsible.

Following the incident, three police officers, including a Sub-Inspector (SI), have been withdrawn from their posts as part of the initial action.

Naim Hasan holds the record for the youngest player to take a five-wicket haul on Test debut and is scheduled to tour Zimbabwe later this month.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[re-digs Cox's Bazar canal]] his father opened 48 years ago
headline: PM Tarique Rahman re-digs Cox's Bazar canal his father opened 48 years ago
summary: The Prime Minister inaugurated the re-excavation of Patali Canal, mirroring a historic moment from 1979 when late president Ziaur Rahman first dug the waterway.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited Cox's Bazar on Saturday, where he inaugurated the re-excavation of the Patali Canal. Braving heavy rain, the Prime Minister picked up a spade to formally launch the work, mirroring the action of his father, late president Ziaur Rahman, in November 1979.

The 8-km canal is expected to benefit around 40,000 people once completed. Local MP Lutfur Rahman Kajol noted that the original development of the canal nearly five decades ago had drawn international attention and sparked a 'green revolution' in the rural economy.

The canal had originally brought 12,000 hectares of uncultivated land under farming, but fell into disuse after five to six years due to neglect and silting. Parts of the canal had also fallen under illegal encroachment, leaving farmers without irrigation water for years.

The Prime Minister was accompanied by several ministers, including Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and Water Resources Minister Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee. Over a thousand villagers gathered along the canal bank in the rain to welcome the PM.
Local farmers, including Jahed Ali, expressed relief, stating that the restoration of the waterway will ensure they no longer have to worry about irrigation water for their crops.
caption:
A historic return to the roots. PM Tarique Rahman re-digs a canal his father opened 48 years ago in Cox's Bazar.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited Cox's Bazar on Saturday, where he inaugurated the re-excavation of the Patali Canal. Braving heavy rain, the Prime Minister picked up a spade to formally launch the work, mirroring the action of his father, late president Ziaur Rahman, in November 1979.

The 8-km canal is expected to benefit around 40,000 people once completed. Local MP Lutfur Rahman Kajol noted that the original development of the canal nearly five decades ago had drawn international attention and sparked a 'green revolution' in the rural economy.

The canal had originally brought 12,000 hectares of uncultivated land under farming, but fell into disuse after five to six years due to neglect and silting. Parts of the canal had also fallen under illegal encroachment, leaving farmers without irrigation water for years.

The Prime Minister was accompanied by several ministers, including Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and Water Resources Minister Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee. Over a thousand villagers gathered along the canal bank in the rain to welcome the PM.

Local farmers, including Jahed Ali, expressed relief, stating that the restoration of the waterway will ensure they no longer have to worry about irrigation water for their crops.
